newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Murders of minors soar in Sao Paulo - report.
newsitem.headline: Murders of minors soar in Sao Paulo - report.

text.p: Murders of children aged between seven and 16 in Brazil's biggest city Sao Paulo soared to 239 in the first five months of the year, a newspaper said on Saturday.
A survey by Sao Paulo police found 91 percent of the victims were involved in the city's booming trade in crack and cocaine, daily Correio Braziliense said.
"The number is impressive because in all of 1996, 337 children were murdered," said police inspector Elisabete Ferreira who heads a unit dedicated to crimes against minors.

Eighty-five percent of the victims came from shanty-towns and most had dropped out of school. "In the streets they met other adolescents and learned to steal, to take and sell drugs and to join gangs," the police officer said.

Of the 239 minors killed so far this year, 38 were girls and the survey found that an increasing number of them had been tortured and sexually abused before being murdered, Ferreira told the newspaper.
